# Bola Ahmed Tinubu, 2024: 3B.8 research note

Bottom line: there is some evidence of tolerance for protest and dialogue, but the dominant 2024 pattern is coercive crowd control, threat framing, treason/cybercrime charges, and selective punishment that chilled dissent.

## Positive / mitigating evidence

- [Tinubu says protests are part of democracy, but the government will not condone destruction](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-receives-u-s-ambassador-underscores-importance-of-sustaining-democracy-its-norms-and-institutions/) — State House, July 25, 2024. Tinubu publicly stated that protests are part of democracy while drawing a line against destruction of lives and property. This is a mild pro-tolerance signal, though it does not show a durable protection of protest rights. Question IDs: `3B.8`; other: `3B.3`, `3B.6`.

- [Tinubu asks protesters to suspend demonstrations, seeks dialogue](https://www.thecable.ng/breaking-tinubu-asks-protesters-to-suspend-demonstrations-seeks-dialogue/) — TheCable, August 4, 2024. Tinubu asked protesters to pause demonstrations to “create room for dialogue” and said he had heard them “loud and clear.” This is the strongest direct evidence for allowing dissent through de-escalation, but it was temporary and came amid a broader crackdown. Question IDs: `3B.8`; other: `3B.6`, `3B.1`.

- [President Tinubu’s Broadcast on the Nationwide Protest](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-broadcast-on-the-nationwide-protest/) — State House, August 4, 2024. Tinubu acknowledged that many protesters had legitimate hopes for a better country and told law enforcement to protect lives and property responsibly. This is partial tolerance of dissent, but it stops short of an unambiguous rights-protective stance. Question IDs: `3B.8`; other: `3B.6`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`.

- [Nigeria security forces deploy, government offers dialogue as protests loom](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/nigeria-security-forces-deploy-government-offers-dialogue-as-protests-loom-3546462) — Reuters via Investing.com, July 31, 2024. Reuters reported that the government said it was open to dialogue even as security forces deployed in major cities. This is mixed evidence, but it does show a public offer of dialogue rather than only suppression. Question IDs: `3B.8`; other: `3B.6`, `3B.5`.

- [Tinubu backed state policing as a way to improve accountability and civil liberties](https://statehouse.gov.ng/my-resolve-to-enhance-nigerias-security-unwavering-president-tinubu/) — State House, April 22, 2024. Tinubu presented state policing as a way to improve accountability and safeguard civil liberties. This is indirect support for non-abusive governance, though it is policy rhetoric rather than an operational guarantee. Question IDs: `3B.8`; other: `3B.4`, `3B.5`.

## Negative evidence

- [Nigeria: Police used excessive force to violently quash #Endbadgovernance protests](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/nigeria-police-used-excessive-force-to-violently-quash-endbadgovernance-protests/) — Amnesty International, November 28, 2024. Amnesty reported live ammunition, killings, mass detentions, and torture during the August protests, and said authorities denied wrongdoing. This is the clearest evidence that peaceful protest was not protected in practice. Question IDs: `3B.8`; other: `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.5`, `3B.6`.

- [Nigeria: Protesters charged with treason](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/06/nigeria-protesters-charged-treason) — Human Rights Watch, September 6, 2024. HRW said protesters, including children, were held for long periods and charged with treason, with due-process concerns. This is strong evidence of selective punishment and chilling of dissent. Question IDs: `3B.8`; other: `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.5`, `3B.6`.

- [Nigeria charges protesters with treason, inciting military](https://theprint.in/world/nigeria-charges-protesters-with-treason-inciting-military/2249248/) — Reuters via ThePrint, September 2, 2024. Prosecutors alleged protesters intended to destabilize the country and incite mutiny. This is strong negative evidence because it recast protest as a security threat rather than a protected political act. Question IDs: `3B.8`; other: `3B.5`, `3B.6`.

- [Nigeria charges 76, including minors, with treason after August protests](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/nigeria-charges-76-including-minors-with-treason-after-august-protests-3698000) — Reuters via Investing.com, November 1, 2024. Reuters reported the case expanded to 76 defendants, including minors. That strengthens the reading of punitive escalation and selective punishment after protest. Question IDs: `3B.8`; other: `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.5`.

- [Nigerian police teargas protesters, arrest dozens](https://theprint.in/world/nigerian-police-teargas-protesters-arrest-dozens/2206531/) — Reuters via ThePrint, August 3, 2024. Police used tear gas and arrests to disperse protesters trying to march on government offices. This looks more like intimidation and restriction than neutral crowd management. Question IDs: `3B.8`; other: `3B.5`, `3B.6`.

- [Nigeria’s police chief warns against “Kenyan-style” protests](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Nigeria-s-police-chief-warns-against-Kenyan-style-protests-47446946/) — Reuters via MarketScreener, July 23, 2024. The police chief framed the coming protests as a security threat before they began. This is indirect but relevant negative evidence for a chilling political climate. Question IDs: `3B.8`; other: `3B.6`, `3B.5`.

- [Nigeria: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/nigeria/freedom-net/2024) — Freedom House, 2024. Freedom House said the Cybercrimes Act’s cyberstalking provision had been used against journalists and activists. This is negative evidence of chilling surveillance / legal pressure on dissent. Question IDs: `3B.8`; other: `3B.5`, `3B.3`.

- [Nigeria police charge 4 journalists with cybercrimes for corruption reporting](https://cpj.org/2024/10/nigeria-police-charge-4-journalists-with-cybercrimes-for-corruption-reporting/) — Committee to Protect Journalists, October 3, 2024. CPJ reported that four journalists were charged under the Cybercrimes Act despite the February reform. This supports the view that security-law tools were used to pressure critical speech. Question IDs: `3B.8`; other: `3B.5`, `3B.3`.

- [Nigeria considers tough penalties for subversive acts under proposed law](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/nigeria-considers-tough-penalties-for-subversive-acts-under-proposed-law-3571782) — Reuters via Investing.com, August 14, 2024. Reuters reported a proposed Counter Subversion Bill that critics said was aimed at cracking down on dissent after the protests, later withdrawn. The proposal itself is negative evidence of an intent to narrow protest space. Question IDs: `3B.8`; other: `3B.5`, `3B.6`.

## Assessment

- There is some evidence of dialogue and rhetorical acceptance of protest.
- The stronger and more concrete evidence is negative: protest policing, treason charges, cybercrime charges against journalists, and proposals that would have punished dissent more harshly.
- On balance, Tinubu did **not** clearly protect peaceful protest and dissent from retaliation or selective punishment in 2024.

## Search gap

- I did not find strong evidence of a stable, rights-protective system for permitting protest and community organization.
- I also did not find reliable evidence of systematic surveillance policy specifically designed to chill civil society beyond the Cybercrimes Act / cyberstalking misuse pattern.
- Most of the available record concerns the August protests; I found less direct evidence about ordinary community organization outside the protest context.
